newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June S&P 500s perk up late, end above 800.00.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June S&P 500s perk up late, end above 800.00.

text.p: U.S. June Standard and Poor's 500 futures perked up late to end strongly higher after languishing in a pre-FOMC lull earlier.
A firm Treasury bond futures close persuaded players who got short on the earlier declines to cover their positions, traders said.
June S&Ps breached 800.00 resistance late to top out at 802.20, the highest price in almost a week.
The late rally sharpened the focus on Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, where many predict a 25-basis point federal funds target hike to 5.5 percent from 5.25.
Because a rate hike has been factored into the market, traders said a relief rally could materialize late on Tuesday.

"Bonds closing strong started this thing off, and then it just took off higher," one S&P 500 futures trader said. He said a 25-basis-point rate hike was completely factored into the market. One trader said rate-hike reaction would be minimal, but said no change in rates could send stocks and bonds tumbling.
"I think the bond market is demanding a rate hike," he said. He said June S&Ps could dip to 782.00 to 782.50 if rates remain unchanged.
Many traders had expected quiet trade on Tuesday heading into the FOMC results, but the late rally today could keep trade choppy or jittery on Tuesday morning, they said.
"Now that you are at these levels, it's a whole new ball game," one S&P trader said. He said some late S&P strength may have been tied to rolling from technology stocks.
June Nasdaq 100 futures cut much of their steep losses in afternoon trade, but still ended lower.
"No doubt (the Nasdaq recovery) helped, but we did so much better that it looked to us at times like people were rolling out of tech stocks and into S&Ps," the trader said.
Traders noted estimated June S&P volume of 70,000 contracts on Monday, versus 58,726 contracts traded on Friday.
Nikkei 225 futures closed on the highs but still lower.
"There was pretty good volume in there -- maybe 1,100 contracts overall," a Nikkei trader said.

At the close, June S&P 500 futures were up 9.50 points at 801.15, Nasdaq 100s were 4.35 lower at 818.40, KCBT Value Line futures were up 3.00 points at 711.60, Nikkei 225 index futures fell 375.0 to 18,295 and Midcap 400s fell 0.40 points to 262.10.
